source_reconstruction.general_proposition_91: For general A, Maynard groups tuples by q, bounds their number by O(tau_(3k)(q)), and combines Hypothesis 1(1) and (3) by Cauchy-Schwarz.
source_reconstruction.proposition_94_omission: The equation-(9.52) paragraph says only that the same argument applies in k+1 dimensions.
source_reconstruction.actual_application_specialization: FGKMT sets A=Z, alpha=2, theta=1/3 and invokes Proposition 9.4 with D=1 and xi=theta/10.
source_reconstruction.critical_correction: For the actual consecutive-integer interval, E_q^(1)<=1 exactly for every q and residue. Consequently the P94 distribution child does not require the unknown general Hypothesis 1(1) or (3) multipliers. This does not remove Hypothesis 1(2) from Proposition 9.2 or the full theorem.

finite_lemmas.result: For N consecutive integers, every residue count differs from N/q by at most 1.

For fixed squarefree q, each free prime has at most 3(k+1) assignments: one of k+1 coordinates and d-only, e-only, or both. The tuple multiplicity is at most tau_(3(k+1))(q), with no hidden multiplier.
sum_(q<Q) tau_a(q) <= Q(1+log Q)^a for Q>1 and integer a>=1.
With z=x^xi and C0=W0/phi(W0), |tilde_lambda_d0|<=C0*z; the predecessor sharp gate gives tilde_lambda_1>=xi*log(x)/2.

The total equation-(9.52) error over all v0 is at most rho_94 times the canonical Proposition 9.4 right-hand-side scale, where log(rho_94) is the explicit expression in theory 30 and source/h1b2a2_proposition94_distribution.py. A closed-form sufficient log-x gate makes rho_94<=1.

symbolic_bounds.W0: D=1 and log W0 < 4k^2+k log 2+alpha(2k+1) log x

symbolic_bounds.decay: R^2*x^(4xi)/x <= x^(-(1-16theta/15)); hence theta<15/16 is required by this deliberately coarse proof
